atsCheck.metaTitle: Free ATS check for your CV
atsCheck.metaDescription: Check for free whether your CV can be read by applicant tracking systems (ATS): a score out of 100 and what to fix, no sign-up.
atsCheck.title: Free ATS check: can recruiters' software read your CV?
atsCheck.intro: Many companies sort applications with software (an ATS). Upload your CV as a PDF: you get a score out of 100 and a list of points to fix.
atsCheck.privacy: Your file is read during the analysis, then forgotten: it is neither stored nor sent to an AI. No account needed.
atsCheck.hint: or drop it here · PDF up to 5 MB

verdict.good: Your CV is easy for recruitment software to read.
verdict.ok: Your CV is readable, but a few fixes would improve your chances.
verdict.low: Recruitment software may misread your CV: fix the points in red first.

errors.NOT_PDF: This file is not a PDF. Save your CV as a PDF, then try again.
errors.TOO_LARGE: This file is larger than 5 MB. Save your CV as a lighter PDF.
errors.UNREADABLE: This PDF could not be read: it may be password-protected or damaged.
errors.RATE_LIMITED: You have run many checks in a short time. Try again in an hour.
errors.generic: The analysis did not complete. Try again in a moment.

readable.pass: Your CV's text can be read by software.
readable.fail: No readable text: your CV seems to be an image or a scan. Recruitment software will read nothing, so recreate it with real text.

email.fail: No email address found: add it at the top of your CV, as text (not in an image).

phone.warn: No phone number found: add it so recruiters can call you back.

experience.fail: No “Experience” section found: use a simple heading such as “Work experience”.

education.fail: No “Education” section found: use a simple heading such as “Education”.

skills.warn: No “Skills” section: add one with the keywords of your job.

length.warn: Length to review ({words} words): aim for 200 to 900 words.
length.fail: Unsuitable length ({words} words): aim for 200 to 900 words.

pages.pass: {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}: perfect.
pages.warn: 3 pages: that's long, try to fit it on 2 pages.
pages.fail: {pages} pages: far too long, aim for 1 or 2 pages.

dates.warn: Few dates: give the start and end of each job and course.

results.warn: No figures: when you can, add real numbers (clients, projects, percentages).

characters.warn: Some characters cannot be read (icons or decorative fonts): use a standard font.

atsCheck.aboutText: An ATS (Applicant Tracking System) is the software that receives applications at many companies and recruitment agencies. It reads the text of your CV, files it in a profile and helps the recruiter find candidates who match the job. If it misreads your CV, your application can go unnoticed.
atsCheck.checksText: The check reads your CV the way software would: is the text readable, are your contact details found, do the main sections have clear headings, are the length and dates suitable? It does not judge the content of your experience.
atsCheck.tip1: Save your CV as a PDF from your word processor: never as a photo or scan.
atsCheck.tip3: Put your contact details as text at the top of the page, not in an image header.
atsCheck.tip4: Reuse the keywords from the job ad that truly match your experience.
atsCheck.tip5: Choose a standard font and a clean layout, on one or two pages.
atsCheck.a1: Yes, with no sign-up. Only the number of checks per hour is limited, to prevent abuse.
atsCheck.a2: No. The file is read during the analysis, then forgotten: it is neither stored nor sent to an AI.
atsCheck.q3: Does a two-column CV work with an ATS?
atsCheck.a3: Often yes, but some software mixes up the columns. A single-column layout with simple headings is the safest.
atsCheck.q4: Does a good score guarantee an interview?
atsCheck.a4: No: the check makes sure your CV is readable, not that your profile matches the job. Tailor your CV to each job ad too.
